quotes.text: Metrics are the numbers on a dashboard, like a server sitting at eighty percent memory right now. Logs are the detailed story of what happened, like who signed in, what they opened, and what broke right after.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear beginner distinction between metrics and logs.

quotes.text: a log is only as useful as your ability to search it, and a cabinet full of records you never open is just storage.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable framing of why collection alone creates no value.

quotes.text: Teams that treat the workspace like a junk drawer end up paying for a junk drawer. The right fix is the one we mentioned earlier, which is to filter and reshape data before it's stored.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete cost advice: filter data at ingestion.

quotes.text: The honest limit is that a default isn't forever, and finding something later only works if you set the retention before you need it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Actionable warning about planning retention in advance.

takeaways: Log Analytics is the log half of Azure Monitor: a workspace whose tables collect records from Azure, other clouds, servers and applications.
KQL turns millions of records into answers, and the same language works in Microsoft Sentinel and Defender advanced hunting.
Cost and retention depend on what you collect, which table plan you choose and how long you keep data, so filter early and set retention before you need it.
hook: Every sign-in, file open and error is already being recorded somewhere, but few teams know how to read it or what it costs to keep. This episode explains Log Analytics for Azure and Microsoft 365 beginners: workspaces, tables, KQL, table plans and retention. You will know what to collect, how to query it and how to keep the bill under control.
